stem: A perioperative nurse performs surgical hand antisepsis using an antimicrobial soap before donning sterile gloves. Which instruction is consistent with current CDC guidance?

options.A: Scrub hands and forearms for the manufacturer's recommended time, usually 2 to 6 minutes
options.B: Scrub for at least 10 minutes regardless of the product used
options.C: Scrub for about 20 seconds because surgical antisepsis uses the same timing as routine handwashing
options.D: Use no defined product instructions because duration does not affect surgical hand antisepsis

rationale: CDC guidance for surgical hand antisepsis states that when an antimicrobial soap is used, the hands and forearms should be scrubbed for the length of time recommended by the manufacturer, usually 2 to 6 minutes; long scrub times such as 10 minutes are not necessary. The timing for routine handwashing is not substituted for surgical antisepsis, and product instructions remain relevant. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Apply current CDC surgical hand antisepsis guidance by following the antimicrobial soap manufacturer's recommended scrub time, usually 2 to 6 minutes.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
source_version_date: CDC page dated 2024-02-27; current page accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Follow hand hygiene recommendations for surgery — when using an antimicrobial soap: scrub hands and forearms for the length of time recommended by the manufacturer, usually 2–6 minutes; long scrub times such as 10 minutes are not needed
source_claim_supported: For surgical hand antisepsis with antimicrobial soap, follow the manufacturer's recommended scrub duration, usually 2 to 6 minutes; unnecessarily long scrub times are not recommended.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: apply infection-prevention practices and aseptic/sterile technique during client care
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — surgical hand antisepsis
correction_summary: Corrected the source item's 2–5 minute range to the current CDC wording: manufacturer-recommended duration, usually 2–6 minutes, specifically for antimicrobial soap. Explicitly distinguished this from alcohol-based surgical hand antisepsis, which follows the product's instructions, and removed the padded 30-minute narrative.
audit_findings: A exactly matches current CDC guidance. B incorrectly imposes an unnecessary universal 10-minute scrub; C imports routine handwashing timing into surgical antisepsis; D disregards required product instructions. By specifying antimicrobial soap, the item avoids ambiguity with alcohol-based surgical products. No second answer or unsupported numeric precision remains.
